from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Any periodic signal is a sum of sine waves.",
            "Think of a guitar chord as individual notes.",
            "We can break complex sounds into simple parts."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Musical Instrument Analogy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Pre-create elements
        # Waves: complex (#FF00FF), components (#00FFFF)
        complex_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x) + 0.3 * np.sin(2*x) + 0.2 * np.sin(3*x), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#FF00FF")
        comp1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#00FFFF")
        comp2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(2*x), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#00FFFF")
        comp3 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.2 * np.sin(3*x), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#00FFFF")
        
        note = Text("♪", color="#FFFF00", font_size=48)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(complex_wave, comp1, comp2, comp3), "A1", "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(complex_wave), Create(comp1), Create(comp2), Create(comp3))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(note, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(note))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Synthesize complex wave from simpler ones (just a simple shift or visual indicator)
        self.play(comp1.animate.shift(UP*0.5), comp2.animate.shift(DOWN*0.5), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Language of Orthogonality", [
            "Periodic functions repeat their values regularly.",
            "Sine and cosine waves are mathematically orthogonal.",
            "This allows us to find individual frequency components."
        ])

        # Define elements
        v1 = Vector([1, 0, 0], color="#00FF00")
        v2 = Vector([0, 1, 0], color="#00FF00")
        label_v1 = Text("v1", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        label_v2 = Text("v2", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        
        v3 = Vector([0.7, 0.7, 0], color="#FF0000")
        proj_line = DashedLine(v3.get_end(), [0.7, 0, 0], color="#FF0000")
        proj_line2 = DashedLine(v3.get_end(), [0, 0.7, 0], color="#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(v1, v2), "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(label_v1, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(label_v2, "B3")
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2), Write(label_v1), Write(label_v2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # (Orthogonality already implied by visual setup)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(v3, "C3")
        self.play(GrowArrow(v3))
        self.play(Create(proj_line), Create(proj_line2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: The Fourier Series Formula", [
            "The Fourier series is an infinite harmonic sum.", 
            "Coefficients act like volume knobs for frequencies.", 
            "Adding harmonics gradually sharpens the signal shape."
        ])

        # Formula construction
        formula = MathTex(
            "f(t) = \\frac{a_0}{2} + \\sum_{n=1}^{\\infty} \\left( a_n \\cos(n \\omega t) + b_n \\sin(n \\omega t) \\right)",
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The Fourier series is an infinite harmonic sum.
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Coefficients act like volume knobs for frequencies.
        an_bn_highlight = formula[0][8:10] # a_n
        bn_highlight = formula[0][17:19]  # b_n
        self.play(
            Indicate(an_bn_highlight, color="#00FFFF"),
            Indicate(bn_highlight, color="#00FFFF"),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Adding harmonics gradually sharpens the signal shape.
        sum_highlight = formula[0][7:8] # sum
        self.play(
            Indicate(sum_highlight, color="#FFFF00"),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Calculating the Components", [
            "We use integrals to filter specific frequencies.", 
            "The integral measures the area of overlap.", 
            "This technique extracts individual rhythmic components."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        complex_signal = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(2*x) + 0.5*np.cos(5*x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        basis_func = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(2*x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=GRAY)
        integral_symbol = MathTex(r"\int", font_size=48)
        
        # Grid positioning
        self.place_in_area(complex_signal, "A2", "B5")
        self.place_in_area(basis_func, "C2", "D5")
        self.place_at_grid(integral_symbol, "E3")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(FadeIn(integral_symbol))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.play(FadeIn(complex_signal), FadeIn(basis_func))
        self.play(Indicate(complex_signal), Indicate(basis_func))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        coeff_text = Text("Result: 0.85", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(coeff_text, "F4")
        self.play(Write(coeff_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Data Compression", [
            "Fourier series are essential for modern data compression.",
            "We keep only the most important coefficients.",
            "Discarding the rest saves significant storage space."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a high-resolution signal curve.
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 2*PI, 0.5], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        signal = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + 0.5*np.sin(3*x), color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(signal, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(signal))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Select and remove lower-magnitude high-frequency Fourier components.
        # Representing high freq component as a secondary wave
        high_freq_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2*np.sin(10*x), color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(high_freq_wave, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        self.play(FadeIn(high_freq_wave))
        self.play(FadeOut(high_freq_wave))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the reconstructed (compressed) signal.
        reconstructed = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(reconstructed, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Transform(signal, reconstructed))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Pure Fourier Series: Breaking Down Waves

sections.title: The Hook: The Musical Instrument Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the concept that any complex periodic signal (a 'sound') can be decomposed into simple, pure sine waves. Analogy: A guitar chord is just a collection of individual notes played together.
sections.example: Visualize a digital synthesizer layering three different pure sine waves to mimic the sound of a 'meowing' cat.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Orthogonality
sections.content: Briefly define periodic functions and the concept of orthogonality of sine/cosine. Explain that these waves act like 'axes' in a coordinate system, allowing us to find individual components.
sections.example: Use a 2D graph animation showing how a vector (a complex wave) is projected onto the X (sine) and Y (cosine) axes.

sections.title: The Core Concept: The Fourier Series Formula
sections.content: Present the Fourier series equation as an infinite sum of harmonics. Explain the role of the coefficients (a_n, b_n) as the 'volume knobs' for each frequency component.
sections.example: An animation showing a square wave being built: starting with one sine wave, then adding the 3rd, 5th, and 7th harmonics until the shape sharpens.

sections.title: Calculating the Components
sections.content: Explain the Integral method. This is how we 'filter' out specific frequencies from a complex signal. Emphasize that we are calculating the 'area of overlap'.
sections.example: A visual 'sieve' moving across a complex heartbeat signal to extract the primary rhythmic frequency.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Data Compression
sections.content: Summarize how Fourier Series are used in modern tech, such as JPEG or MP3, by keeping only the most important 'coefficients' and discarding the rest to save memory.
sections.example: A side-by-side comparison of a high-resolution image of a dog vs. a compressed version, demonstrating how keeping the 'first 5 terms' maintains the recognizable shape.
